_comment: AMOUNT-BASED APPROVAL THRESHOLDS. Policy CONFIGURATION, not policy rules.
The PAP pushes this document into OPA at data.agentic_iam.config.loan, and
policies/loan/amount.rego reads it. The split is deliberate: what an amount
MEANS is a security rule that a reviewer reads in Rego; what the numbers ARE
is a lending decision that a risk committee changes without touching a rule.
Nothing in Python reads these values. There is no `if amount > x` anywhere in
the application -- the PIP establishes the amount from the resource record and
OPA decides what to do about it.
FAILING CLOSED: if this document is absent from the engine, loan/amount.rego
denies with LOAN_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED rather than falling through. An
unconfigured threshold must never read as 'no limit'.
Amounts are minor-unit-free whole rupees (INR).
agent_autonomous_limit_inr -- at or below this, an agent holding a valid
capability credential scoped to loan_applications may record the decision
on its own authority. No human is involved, because referring every
trivial loan to a person produces rubber-stamping, which is worse than not
asking.
single_approver_limit_inr -- above the autonomous limit and at or below
this, ONE authorized LOAN_OFFICER must approve. This is the loan officer's
personal approval authority.
Above single_approver_limit_inr -- TWO distinct authorized humans. The same
person cannot satisfy both.
Which human role may approve a loan decision. Stated here so the role and
the amount bands are configured together; the RULE that reads it lives in
policies/control_plane/humans.rego.
Maker-checker. When true, the officer named as submitted_by on the
application may not sign it off. Turning it off is a deliberate,
reviewable configuration change rather than something a code path decides.
